text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein to oversee celebrations for handover of 30 million cubic metres from Israel's Sea of Galilee today.
- Minister of State for Information Samir Mutawae says the government is open to dialogue with journalists over Jordan's new press restrictions.
- Minister of Education Munzir al-Masri says students who participated in Jordan's independence day and army day celebrations will be excused end of year exams.
- Minister of Transport and Telecommunications Bassam al-Saket says rail link between Israel and Jordan must wait, delayed until financial benefit is clear and funding is available.
- Cabinet to discuss today fixing bonuses for professional workers in state and private sector.
- Military trial of soldier who shot Israeli schoolgirls starts today. Defendant faces death penalty.
- Parliamentary committee for foreign affairs calls for Arab summit to study Turkish incursion into northern Iraq.
- Returnees from the Gulf War start to receive their compensation.
- Three plans for trains linking Jordan and Israel between Mafraq, Haifa, Aqaba and Ashdod. Minister says regional plans need executive decisions and financing otherwise they remain just wishes.
- Finance Minister Suleiman al-Hafez details debt rescheduling with Paris Club. Jordan given higher privilege for swap deals.
